ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that $\angle BDC=142^\circ$, $\angle B=34^\circ$, and $\angle C=28^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle A$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Construct ray AE passing through points A and D, \\
$\because$ $\angle CDE = \angle CAD + \angle C$, $\angle BDE = \angle BAD + \angle B$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle BDC = \angle CDE + \angle BDE = \angle CAD + \angle C + \angle BAD + \angle B = 142^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAB + 34^\circ + 28^\circ = 142^\circ$, \\
$\therefore$ $\angle CAB = \boxed{80^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure A is on the left side, C is on the upper right, B is on the lower right, and D is located near the inside of the figure; visible are line segments AD, AC, AB, CD, BD, and AD divides the desired ∠A into ∠BAD and ∠CAD. The problem gives ∠BDC=142°, ∠B=34°, ∠C=28°. Reasoning: According to the method, extend AD through D into ray DE. In the triangle ACD formed by the line segments, by the exterior angle theorem, ∠CDE = ∠CAD + ∠C. In the triangle ABD formed by the line segments, by the exterior angle theorem, ∠BDE = ∠BAD + ∠B. In the figure ∠BDC is composed of adjacent ∠CDE and ∠BDE, so 142° = ∠BDC = ∠CDE + ∠BDE = (∠CAD + 28°) + (∠BAD + 34°). Therefore ∠BAD + ∠CAD = 142° - 28° - 34° = 80°. And ∠A = ∠BAD + ∠CAD, so ∠A = 80°.
